title: Scalar text policy expands into every overlapping display window
fault_primitive: MongoDB collection validator with unit-stride nested codepoint ranges
incident_class: Database validation policy compilation regression causing write amplification
symptoms: Pods remain Running and Ready. Valid post inserts consume excessive database CPU, compose requests become slow, and end-user throughput falls below target. Cached timeline reads can remain fast. MongoDB CPU rises sharply; traces and slow operations lead to post insertion without naming the expensive collection policy.
why_hard: The configuration is native collection metadata, absent from Deployment/ConfigMap dumps and ordinary document dumps. Valid documents are accepted, so there is no schema rejection naming the policy. The expensive work comes from overlapping text windows rather than larger documents, additional traffic, missing indexes, or unhealthy dependencies. Restarting application pods and changing connection pools cannot remove the durable validator. Each apparent text limit is reasonable; the defect is the cardinality of the candidate boundaries.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treating database CPU as evidence of a missing read index
Increasing RPC deadlines or connection counts
Restarting RPC services or flushing caches
Inspecting documents without inspecting collection validation options
Relaxing the byte or token limits while leaving both unit-stride ranges in place
mitigation_summary: Read the live validator and extract its byte, codepoint, and token limits. Replace overlapping-substring checks with one check of each limit against the complete text, preserving independent policy clauses. No original manifests or saved state are required.

RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "curl -s http://10.96.195.94:16686/api/services; curl -s http://10.96.90.179/api/v1/query --get --data-urlencode 'query=rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=\"social-network\",pod=~\"post-storage-mongodb.*\"}[1m])'"
SAYS: The collection validator was checking every substring of each post, making inserts unnecessarily expensive. I replaced it with equivalent checks on the full text, preserving the limits and strict validation. I’m verifying latency and request success before submitting. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n social-network deployment/post-storage-mongodb -- mongo --quiet post --eval 'var a=db.serverStatus().opLatencies.writes; sleep(10000); var b=db.serverStatus().opLatencies.writes; printjson({writes:b.ops-a.ops,meanWriteLatencyMs:(b.latency-a.latency)/(b.ops-a.ops)/1000}
SAYS: MongoDB writes now average 0.52 ms, CPU usage has fallen to 20 millicores, and a timeline request returned HTTP 200 in 21 ms. I’m submitting the mitigation for sustained validation. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "curl -sS -X POST http://host.docker.internal:8000/submit -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"solution\":\"\"}'"
SAYS: Fixed the expensive MongoDB validator while preserving its validation limits.  Writes now average 0.52 ms; a timeline request succeeded in 21 ms. Submitted the required empty solution, and the endpoint accepted it for validation.
